title: Bulgur-Stuffed Chard Rolls with Lemon Sauce
subtitle: with pomegranate and cherry tomatoes
description: Young chard leaves rolled around a bulgur, herb and dried cranberry filling, then baked in a parcel with a lemon and pomegranate sauce.

steps.text: Cut off the bottom third of the chard leaves and use only the wide green part (keep the thick white-veined part in the fridge for stews or salads).
Boil a large pot of water with the half lemon and blanch the chard leaves for 30-60 seconds. They should be soft enough not to tear when rolled. Drain and keep in a bowl of cold water.

Place the bulgur in a bowl, fill with warm tap water, stir and pour off the water. Repeat twice more. Drain, leaving 2 tablespoons of liquid, and let the bulgur swell for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Saute the chopped spring onion in the oil for 2 minutes. Add the garlic and parsley and stir for 1 minute. Add the bulgur and the rest of the filling ingredients and fry for 3 minutes, stirring.

Lay a chard leaf on the work surface with the veined side up. Place a spoonful of filling on it, fold in the sides, fold the bottom edge over and roll up. If a leaf is torn, overlap two leaves and roll as usual.

Lay a long piece of kitchen string across a small baking dish and cover with baking paper. Lightly oil the paper and pack the rolls tightly on it, seam side down. Scatter the halved cherry tomatoes, halved garlic cloves and pomegranate seeds between the rolls.
Mix the sauce ingredients and pour over. Close the paper and tie with the string.
Bake for 40 minutes. Serve hot or at room temperature.
